questions.question: If in a code language, ROHAN is coded as 3136 and SHYAM is coded as 4356, then how will you code RAM?
questions.solution:
**The table is alphabets place value:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/259d8630a9ac11653540776fb8c878efe7c7e39d2fafd27847036c083bb6c14d.png] 

The pattern followed here is:

**(Sum of the positional values of the letters)² = number.**

**ROHAN** →.

R(18) + O(15) + H(8) + A(1) + N(14) = 18 + 15 + 8 + 1 + 14 = 56

(Sum of the positional values of the letters)² = number

=> (56)² = 3136

**And,**

**SHYAM** →

S(19) + H(8) + Y(25) + A(1) + M(13) = 19 + 8 + 25 + 1 + 13 = 66

(Sum of the positional values of the letters)² = number

=> (66)² = 4356

**Similarly,**

**RAM → **

**R(18) + A(1) + M(13) = 18 + 1 + 13 = 32**

**(Sum of the positional values of the letters)² = number**

**=> (32)² = 1024**

Hence, **RAM** will be written as **“1024”.**

questions.question:
Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series.

p r _ b n _ r q _ n p _ q b _ p _ q _ n

options.text: q, p, b, r, n, r, b
q, b, p, n, r, n, r
q, p, b, r, r, n, n
q, r, n, p, b, r, n

questions.solution:
Given :- p r _ b n _ r q _ n p _ q b _ p _ q _ n

By checking options and substituting accordingly.

**Option (1) q, p, b, r, n, r, b →** p r **__q__** b n **-** **__p__** r q **__b__** n **-** p **__r__** q b **__n__** - p **__r__** q **__b__** n

 ♦ Here p r q b n is repeated itself.

**Option (2)** q, b, p, n, r, n, r → p r **__q__** b n **-** **__b__** r q **__p__** n **-** p **__n__** q b **__r__** **-** p **__n__** q **__r__** n

**Option (3) **q, p, b, r, r, n, n → p r **__q__** b n **-** **__p__** r q **__b__** n **-** p **__r__** q b **__r__** **-** p **__n__** q **__n__** n

**Option (4) **q, r, n, p, b, r, n → p r **__q__** b n **-** **__r__** r q **__n__** n **-** p **__p__** q b **__b__** **-** p **__r__** q **__n__** n

 ♦ Option (1) gives a pattern of **p r q b n** - p r q b n - **p r q b n** - p r q b n.

Hence, **‘****q, p, b, r, n, r, b’ **is the correct answer.

questions.question: There are three books coded as A, B and C. The price of book A is twice the price of book B and one-third the price of book C. If book C costs Rs. 84, then what are the costs of book A and book B, respectively?
questions.solution:
Given:

Three books coded as A, B and C.

1) The price of book A is twice the price of book B

=> A = 2B → eq. 1

2) The price of book A is one-third the price of book C

=> A = 1/3 C → eq. 2

3) Book C costs Rs. 84

Put the value in eq. 2

=> A = 1/3 × 84

**=> A = 28**

Put the value of A in eq 1;

=> A = 2B

=> 28 = 2B

=> B = 28 ÷ 2

**=> B = 14**

Hence, the costs of book A and book B, respectively **“****Rs. 28 and Rs. 14”.**

questions.question:
Arrange the following words in a logical and meaningful order.

1. Eat

2. Rinse

3. Buy

4. Cut

5. Cook
questions.solution:
The logical and meaningful order of the given words is as follows:

**LOGIC:** The words have been arranged according to the stage of vegetable cook.

**3. Buy **→ Firstly we buy vegetables.

**2. Rinse **→ Then we rinse vegetables.

**4. Cut **→ After the rinse vegetables we cuts the vegetables.

**5. Cook **→ Then after cutting we cook the vegetables.

**1. Eat **→ After cooked vegetable we can eat.

Hence, **"****3, 2, 4, 5, 1****"** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some lights are wires.

All appliances are lights.

All bulbs are appliances.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some lights are appliances.

II. Some wires are bulbs.

III. All bulbs are lights.

options.text: Both conclusions I and III follow
Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Statements:

Some lights are wires.

All appliances are lights.

All bulbs are appliances.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/68ab20c3469265cdcaf641b0ea7ed0b6e483166c48c41ac3c9cb59624921b4a3.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some lights are appliances → True (because all appliances are lights so some lights are also appliances)

II. Some wires are bulbs → False (It is possible but not definite)

III. All bulbs are lights → True (because all bulbs are appliances and all appliances are light so all bulbs are also lights)

Hence, “**Both conclusions I and III follow**”.

questions.question:
Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(11, 20, 81)
questions.solution:
The Logic here is as follows:

**(2ⁿd number - 1st Number)² = 3rd Number**

**In **(11, 20, 81)

**(2ⁿd number - 1st Number)² **

= (20 - 11)²

= 9²

= 81 **= 3rd Number**

Now check the all options,

**Option (1) **(36, 28, 25)

**(2ⁿd number - 1st Number)² **

= (28 - 36)²

= (- 8)²

= 64 ≠** 3rd Number**

**Option (2) **(25, 36, 121)

**(2ⁿd number - 1st Number)² **

**= (36 - 25)²**

**= 11²**

**= 121 = 3rd Number**

**Option (3) **(12, 30, 224)

**(2ⁿd number - 1st Number)² **

= (30 - 12)²

= 18²

= 324 ≠** 3rd Number**

**Option (4) **(14, 29, 64)

**(2ⁿd number - 1st Number)² **

= (29 - 14)²

= 15²

= 225 ≠** 3rd Number**

Hence, the correct answer is **"****(25, 36, 121)****".**

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(1, 2, 6)
questions.solution:
The Logic here is as follows:

**(1st number)² + 1st number = 2ⁿd number**

**(2ⁿd number)² + 2ⁿd number = 3rd number**

**In **(1, 2, 6)

(1st number)² + 1st number

=> 1² + 1 = 1 + 1 = 2 **= 2ⁿd number**

(2ⁿd number)² + 2ⁿd number

=> 2² + 2 = 4 + 2 = 6 **= 3rd number**

Now check the all options,

**Option (1) **(10, 20, 40)

(1st number)² + 1st number

=> 10² + 10 = 100 + 10 = 110 **≠ 2ⁿd number**

(2ⁿd number)² + 2ⁿd number

=> 20² + 20 = 400 + 20 = 420 **≠ 3rd number**

**Option 2) **(7, 14, 49)

(1st number)² + 1st number

=> 7² + 7 = 49 + 7 = 56 **≠ 2ⁿd number**

(2ⁿd number)² + 2ⁿd number

=> 14² + 14 = 196 + 14 = 210 **≠ 3rd number**

**Option 3) **(1, 2, 16)

(1st number)² + 1st number

=> 1² + 1 = 1 + 1 = 2 **= 2ⁿd number**

(2ⁿd number)² + 2ⁿd number

=> 2² + 2 = 4 + 2 = 6 **≠ 3rd number**

**Option (4) (5, 30, 930)**

**(1st number)² + 1st number **

**=> 5² + 5 = 25 + 5 = 30 = 2ⁿd number**

**(2ⁿd number)² + 2ⁿd number**

**=> 30² + 30 = 900 + 30 = 930 = 3rd number**

Hence, the correct answer is **"****(5, 30, 930)****".**
